Reduce White Point listing copy vs display engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate system accessibility features with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Reduce White Point on the device — iOS dims bright whites and lowers the intensity of vivid colors so screens feel less harsh for light-sensitive users. Toggle and intensity slider under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → Reduce White Point; optional shortcut under Accessibility → Accessibility Shortcut. System accessibility behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Display brightness and white-point APIs — code that detects Reduce White Point, adapts custom UI for light sensitivity, or ships companion display-comfort demos. Engineering inside the binary — not listing rewrite.
  • Reduce White Point marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app works with Reduce White Point, respects dimmer bright whites, or improves comfort for light-sensitive users. Connect text fields — this page.

  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Reduce White Point.

Reduce White Point-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

White-point and light-comfort marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Reduce White Point in iOS Settings — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 降低白点 for Reduce White Point, with related buyer language around 减弱白点 (soften white point), 白点 (white point), 光线敏感 (light sensitivity), 显示亮度 (display brightness), and 降低白点快捷键 (Reduce White Point shortcut under 辅助功能 → 辅助功能快捷键). Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic 护眼 or medical eye-exam claims that could imply clinical products.

Reduce White Point vs Display Accommodations color filters

Color filters, smart invert, and differentiate without color live under Accessibility → Display & Text Size alongside Reduce White Point — but they adjust display colors and inversion, not white-point dimming specifically. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 颜色滤镜 or 智能反色 when your English source only shows a Reduce White Point intensity slider. See the Display Accommodations listing guide only if color filters are your lead marketing claim.

Reduce White Point vs Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency

Increase Contrast strengthens button, icon, and separator borders — 增强对比度. Reduce Transparency makes sheet backgrounds more opaque — 降低透明度. Reduce White Point dims bright whites and lowers bright-color intensity — 降低白点. If your English gallery shows a contrast or blur toggle, do not upgrade zh-Hans copy to 降低白点 claims unless that is what the frame shows. See the Increase Contrast listing guide or Reduce Transparency listing guide only if those are your lead marketing claims.

Reduce White Point vs Classic Invert and Smart Invert

Classic Invert flips the entire display palette — 反色. Smart Invert inverts UI chrome while preserving photos — 智能反色. Reduce White Point softens bright whites without full inversion — 降低白点. If your English gallery shows an invert toggle, keep zh-Hans copy on inversion vocabulary, not white-point dimming, unless your US page leads with Reduce White Point specifically.

Reduce White Point vs Auto Brightness, True Tone, Night Shift, and Dark Mode

Auto Brightness adjusts overall screen brightness from ambient light sensors. True Tone adjusts white balance — 原彩显示. Night Shift shifts evening warmth — 夜览. Dark Mode changes UI appearance — 深色模式. Reduce White Point dims whites and lowers highlight intensity — 降低白点 — regardless of ambient automation or theme. If your English gallery shows a brightness auto-toggle or dark-theme mockup, do not upgrade zh-Hans copy to 降低白点 claims unless white-point dimming is what the frame depicts.

US pages often show the Reduce White Point intensity slider or Accessibility Shortcut setup for quick toggling. zh-Hans overlay lines should name 强度滑块 or 降低白点快捷键 only when your gallery actually shows those UI elements — not generic "easier on the eyes" claims that could imply unrelated display features.

AppLocale FAQ

Is Reduce White Point the same as Display Accommodations color filters?

No. Reduce White Point dims bright whites and lowers bright-color intensity for light-sensitive users — 降低白点, 减弱白点. Display Accommodations covers color filters, invert colors, and differentiate without color — 颜色滤镜, 反色. See our Display Accommodations listing guide for color-filter marketing copy when that is your lead claim.

Is Reduce White Point the same as Increase Contrast or Reduce Transparency?

No. Increase Contrast boosts UI element contrast — 增强对比度. Reduce Transparency reduces blur and frosted-glass opacity — 降低透明度. Reduce White Point dims bright whites — 降低白点. See our Increase Contrast listing guide or Reduce Transparency listing guide for those claims.

Is Reduce White Point the same as Classic Invert or Smart Invert?

No. Classic Invert and Smart Invert market full-screen or selective color inversion — 反色, 智能反色. Reduce White Point markets dimmer bright whites and lower highlight intensity — 降低白点 — without inverting the entire display.

Is Reduce White Point the same as Auto Brightness, True Tone, Night Shift, or Dark Mode?

No. Auto Brightness, True Tone, Night Shift, and Dark Mode market ambient brightness automation and display color or appearance — 自动亮度, 原彩显示, 夜览, 深色模式. Reduce White Point markets white-point dimming for light sensitivity — 降低白点. See our True Tone listing guide, Night Shift listing guide, or Dark Mode listing guide for display color and appearance copy.
